literal: Always shunning is necessary, along with fame, goodness not-yielding action.
translation: One must always avoid those actions that do not yield both virtue and fame.
modern: புகழையும் நன்மையையும் தராத செயல்களை எக்காலத்திலும் தவிர்த்தல் வேண்டும்.
explanation: This couplet outlines the criteria for pure action. A person must completely avoid any action that fails to bring both moral goodness (virtue) and public esteem (fame). The word 'nanri' refers to the spiritual or moral benefit of an action, while 'pukazh' refers to the honorable reputation it earns in society. If an action does not produce these two positive outcomes, it is deemed unworthy and must be shunned at all times.
